purpose: Native game input decisions: raw scan changes, mutable make/break sequence matching, measured-count calibration, signed direction classification and five word-valued commands per player, with explicit DOS hardware services.

inputs: One borrowed InputState plus mutable InputKeyRecord storage. Control modes/player count are the same front-end/session cells, not independently persistent copies.

Port supplies raw scan byte deliveries, two active-high button-mask groups and x/y counts per controller, with presence information. Counts share a consistent calibration/sample unit; directions are decided natively.
DOS adapter optionally derives those counts from exact port201 status deliveries. Indexed keyboard-byte requests retain all256 index bytes, wrapping record traversal and writable table aliases.
outputs: Previous/current/change scan bytes and packed AX result; candidate states/index and a byte action store on completed record.
Calibrated presence/modes/axes, thresholds ceil(n/2),low16(n+floor(n/2)),low16(2*n), unsigned maximum timeout. Raw word-valued up/down/left/right/action.
Exact ordered IN/OUT/DOS events, BIOS head=tail, installed/restored vectors, preserved/clobbered registers and error/budget prefixes through bridge.
effects: Keyboard record requests read/rebind after every write, retaining mutable sentinel/source/action aliases. Byte actions preserve stale high bytes.
Mapped source words cannot overlap command words for any admitted shifted mode. Their ordinary-RAM reads may be grouped; selected command stores retain original order.
Hardware timing and IRQ/vector delivery are services, with no original code identities or segmented pointers in ordinary native code.
preconditions: Serialized ordinary input/source RAM and disjoint active code/call frame; no claim for MMIO input records or mid-instruction asynchronous IRQ equivalence.
Mapping state/player count remains stable during the call: its command stores do not target count or source words. Explicit event delivery remains at original service points.
Work state starts with native begin functions and resumes only after successful synchronous services. A service error terminates its caller, preserving the returned prefix.
Portable normal modes are FFFF/0/1; bridge also retains raw16-bit shift/sign and unchecked indexed source reads. No bounds clamp is inserted.

indirect.keyboard: KeyboardHandlerVector is initialized to HandleKeyboardScanInterrupt and has no discovered shipped writer. High-score/password entry restores the saved BIOS handler and later reinstalls the game handler. Raw API vector mutations remain platform inputs, not native function pointers.
indirect.chaining: The shipped scan ISR never calls the saved handler. It reads60, processes records and emits PIC EOI; there is no port61/8042 toggle.
indirect.records: A mutable data grammar, not a cheat program or callback table. Record destinations/values select action byte stores; known targets0,2,...18 and unused20.

memory.owner: Existing input owner in GAME/DGROUP. InputState and companion mutable InputKeyRecord storage are views of that owner; no native persistent global copy.
memory.shared: SelectPlayerControls writes both control modes via indexed PlayerOneControlMode+BX. RunMainMenuAndAttractLoop toggles the PlayerCount word with XOR3; KeyboardHandlerVector is statically initialized to the scan ISR, with no discovered shipped writer. Native input projects these fresh.
memory.views: Player-physics/actor code borrows the five command words. actors.h and those units are unchanged.
memory.layout: 34 six-byte records plusFF; three scan/FF bytes,destination,value,candidate. CandidateFF rejects; every other byte is active. Offset/index arithmetic wraps at16/8 bits respectively.
memory.aliases: Action offset20 is an unused word sink; original table can target/overwrite its own bytes when malformed. Raw request binding preserves this. Five commands remain uint16 words: keyboard byte release does not erase old high bytes.

retained: IRQ raw prefixes/breaks are bytes; no BIOS queueing/scan translation or old-handler chain. Only60 IN then20 EOI.

Matcher checks first candidate before any initial sentinel check, uses shared byte index, rejects byFF, wraps survivor count, resets all candidates on completion/no survivors, and does not retry a mismatch as a fresh first byte.
Destination bit1 gates player mode sign; destination/value reread after the mode test. Completed matches reset even when the mode suppresses their action. High action bytes remain stale.

Independent button reads yield masks30/C0. Axis priority1,2,4,else8; a detected axis does not decrementCX. Zero limit means65536 empty decrements, disabled/unlatched axes return the live limit. IncomingIF/DF restored only on normal sample exit.

Calibration forcesIF on, startslimitFFFF and resets only the specified presence/mask/doubled/scratch cells; absent modes, counts and thresholds remain stale. Both axes must discharge for presence. The second sample can overwrite first-stick counts after first-stick thresholds were already stored.
Unsigned doubled-center max after word wrap; signed inclusive low/high classification, low direction wins overlaps. Any nonzero button WORD requests action.

Sampling uses original mode sign; mapping uses sign after low16(mode*2). Thus8000 maps stale stick0 while4000 maps as keyboard despite triggering sampling. Exact count2 visits player1; malformed counts still visit player0.

Wait discards the first scan change, waits a complete retrace, tests buttons before the post-retrace keyboard change, and propagates failure before testing returnedAH. Install/restore flush BIOS head to tail and forceIF on only at their original completion points.
